Skipping would therefore shift the reading frame, and NMD is expected because exon 5 is not near the last exon. This is a prediction, not confirmed by RNA data. Loss of function is an established mechanism for IL7R SCID per the VCEP. gnomAD pLI of 0 does not argue against it, since this is a recessive gene.

aiva_evidence.PVS1: Met at Very Strong under the APC VCEP spec (GN089), which has a modified PVS1 decision tree. VEP shows a frameshift (ENST00000457016, p.Lys1593SerfsTer57, HIGH impact) in the last coding exon (exon 16). Loss of function is the established mechanism (gnomAD pLI=0.99999 and LOEUF=0.355 per gnomad_constraint, though cancer genes are inconclusive on this metric). The exact Figure 1 strength for this codon was not retrieved, so Very Strong is a judgement. A further web search was rate-limited.

aiva_evidence.PVS1: Very Strong under ClinGen Monogenic Diabetes GCK VCEP (GN086). VEP shows a frameshift (p.Ala379GlyfsTer75 on ENST00000345378, equivalent to p.Ala378fs), so the new stop falls around codon 453, in exon 10. The VCEP says PTCs in exon 10 are not expected to undergo NMD, but it applies Very Strong to them anyway, because the α13 helix (p.444-456) is critical and exon 10 PTCs give a MODY phenotype. This is a judgement call, since the stop position is inferred from the VEP frameshift length and not confirmed against exon boundaries. gnomAD LOEUF 0.80 and pLI ~0 do not support LOF intolerance, but the VCEP's gene-specific LOF mechanism takes precedence.

aiva_evidence.PVS1: Canonical splice acceptor variant (c.1066-1G>A, intron 10) per VEP. The PAH VCEP (GN006) gives Very Strong for a canonical splice site predicted to disrupt the reading frame and undergo NMD. I inferred exon 11 skipping would shift the frame from the exon 10/11 boundary, which VCEP lists as frame-preserving only for exons 1, 9 and 10. This inference was not checked against RNA data or an exon-length lookup. PAH LOF is the established mechanism for recessive PKU despite a low gnomAD pLI.

The exon numbering was inferred from overlapping multi-transcript output, so this is not certain. The truncation would remove about 67 of about 1922 aa. aiva_evidence.PVS1: Canonical +1 donor variant. VEP calls it splice_donor_variant (HIGH), and MyVariant maps it to NM_000018.4:c.1827+1G>A. The ClinGen ACADVL VCEP (GN021) says LOF is a known mechanism and that a +1 GT donor variant predicts skipping of the exon 5' of the variant. Exon lengths from Ensembl give c.1827 as the last base of exon 19, the penultimate exon, so exon 19 is predicted to be skipped. The skip is a frameshift in the last exon, so NMD is not predicted. The lost and altered C-terminal region is about 71 aa (about 11% of the 655-aa protein). Applied at Strong, not Very Strong, because NMD is not predicted. No RNA assay was found. SpliceAI timed out. The 76-nt exon length and the 10% estimate are my own calculations from Ensembl exon lengths.

aiva_evidence.PVS1: Met at Very Strong under the ClinGen Platelet Disorders VCEP (GN011), which allows only the SVI decision tree. VEP shows a stop_gained at c.2248C>T (p.Arg750Ter), a null variant in exon 14 of 15 on ENST00000559488. aiva_evidence.PVS1: Met at Strong. VEP shows a frameshift in NM_000156.6 (p.Gly164AlafsTer14), and the ClinGen CCDS VCEP (GN026) applies PVS1 to frameshifts. This is a null variant, and AR loss of function is the established mechanism for GAMT deficiency under the VCEP spec. c.491 is exon 5, within the last 50 bases of the penultimate exon (the spec puts that boundary at c.520). The exon coordinates are from Ensembl; the c.-to-exon mapping is inferred, not confirmed, and the spec does not say which exon c.491 falls in. NMD is therefore predicted to be missed, and the spec downgrades PVS1 in that case. The truncation lands at about codon 177, losing more than 10% of the protein (my estimate from the ~236-aa length, which I did not look up in a tool). Per GN026 this gives PVS1_Strong.
